coordinateSystem: Original unmirrored catalogue coordinates, metres; x=0 left main facade, y=0 garage front. Apply house.metadata transform exactly once.

assumptions: Approximate visual reconstruction from public catalogue raster plans, not execution or BIM documentation.

Room areas, 18 stair rises, 26cm treads, 90cm flight widths, 2.80m ceiling and +3.20m floor come from publisher drawings. Coordinates and door placement are manually traced approximations, typically 10–20cm uncertainty.
Source stair label18×17.68cm sums to3.1824m; visual model uses section+3.20m and uniform18rises.
Published room usable areas on sloped upper floor differ from rectangular floor footprints.
Upper slope follows unchanged exterior roof; interior roof finish thickness and installation void estimated.
The 0.90 m doorway to the private bathroom occupies local x=10.00–10.90 m along the suite partition. Its approximate position is fitted to the traced plan and the junction with the hall wall.

Eight roof windows on the mirrored attic plan have matching openings through the outer roof and the interior lining 45 mm below it. Window centres were digitised from the drawing; glazing size is an estimate. The living room has a solid roof.

Door handing and the two opposing pocket doors in the main suite follow the catalogue floor plans. Values describe the original plan before the site mirror. The main entry, vestibule glass door, concealed pantry front and terrace slider open on approach. Individual paint colours, hardware and pocket tracks are visual design assumptions.

Furniture inventory records approximate source footprints and front direction; beds face from head to foot. Dimensions are visual traces, typically uncertain by15–30cm, not product or execution dimensions.
Room2 upper partition beside the void is solid; the hall alone has a guardrail. Laundry entry is through the side hall; its rear partition is solid as drawn.
Ground main-side glazing traced to y9.23–12.23m; terrace glazing traced to y13.90–16.60m. These refine openings only, preserving the exterior envelope.
Private bathroom front sanitary fixture symbols overlap a rooflight in the public plan. Shower and WC remain explicit approximations; two wall basins follow the visible source.
Furniture under roof slopes uses schematic heights; source footprints and wall contacts are more reliable than catalogue symbol sizes. No unsupported furniture is inferred from rooflight symbols.
Shared upper bathroom doorway refined to y4.64–5.54m against the source opening, leaving the shower approach clear.
Dining seating is the user-requested six-chair override: three chairs per long side, pulled to 6cm from the table edge, instead of eight catalogue chairs.

The mirrored ground-floor drawing supplies usable areas 10.29 and 13.45 m²; their dimensioned footprints include finishes and the low office storage beneath the stairs. The four closed cabinet modules and their individual heights approximate a possible fit-out.

Room 1.1 study desk, chair and wardrobe are a proposed fit-out. The upper hall reading corner and the exposed timber at the crossing of the two roofs interpret the supplied interior view. Member sizes and joints are for visualisation only.

Room 0.8 retains the catalogue folded sofa position. Its assumed pull-out daybed extends toward the room centre to 1.65 m overall depth, including frame and back, with a proposed 1.95 × 1.45 m sleeping area.
